$comment: Which auto-compaction window each train is INTENDED to run with (spec §5.2).
The entrypoint compares this to the effective value resolved from the settings layers and
refuses on disagreement, in both directions. Too small hides context; too large silently
adopts a tier the train was never scoped to.
300000 is the ACCEPTED marathon tier — Kuya, 2026-07-31, on #19: 'accepted as Compy's scoped
marathon tier. It is not the default; routine work remains 150k.' Acceptance settled the tier's
name and status, not its scoping: it is still granted per issue, and `default` stays 150000.
Widening `default` to 300000 to make a refusal go away would be exactly the failure this file
exists to prevent: a routing mistake made invisible by a setting.
Adding an issue here is a decision, not a fix. Record why in `note`.

tiers.note: the marathon tier — run on #15, measured by #16, decided by #19 (accepted by Kuya, 2026-07-31); accepted is not default
the one-selection entrypoint program — Kuya scoped it as marathon-class in the authorizing message (2026-07-31) so future resumes get the tier automatically
